$comment: What an active-time figure is a measurement OF. This is a DIFFERENT contract
from tool-telemetry-contract.v2.json: that one pins the vocabularies a paired
client may put on the wire at ingest, this one names the quantities computed
figures report. Nothing here is ever sent by a client.
The canonical definition is asc-core-be's docs/ACTIVE_TIME.md, section 'The
quantity is the label, not the gap'. This file is the vendored copy, and the
same staleness caveat applies as to the wire contract: nothing in this repo
can reach that one, so re-vendor when the backend's version bumps. The version
assertion in the test is the tripwire that makes a bump impossible to apply
silently.
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE AXIS FROM THE GAP. activeGapMinutes says how a figure
was cut; it does not say what was cut. Two figures sharing a gap can be
incomparable -- coverage and block_coverage are both cut at 30 minutes in
asc-core-be and answer different questions. Two with different gaps can be
legitimately compared: hands_on is cut at 5 here and at 30 there, which is the
same quantity on different corpora. So the gap is deliberately NOT part of the
identity, or the guard would forbid a comparison that is merely delicate.
AGENT-HOURS IS A QUANTITY, NOT A PRESENTATION. docs/ACTIVE_TIME.md says it
twice -- 'Both quantities are real; only the union is elapsed time' and 'A
summed figure may be reported as agent-hours, never as where a week went' --
but its four-name table had no name for the summed form, so the two figures in
this repo that most need distinguishing were the two it could not describe.
In localHandoff.ts, Project.handsOnMinutes is SUMMED across sessions (4.2x wall
clock on the reference machine) while Project.elapsed.handsOnMinutes is
UNIONED. Same spelling, one nesting level apart, different quantities. Both are
deliberate and both are documented; nothing mechanical told them apart until
this file. That is the asc-core-be#194 shape -- two figures sharing a name with
nothing on either distinguishing them -- and it is why a quantity keyed on a
bare field name would be wrong here. Register by (interface, field).
WHAT THE GUARD MAY AND MAY NOT FORBID. Adding or subtracting across differing
quantities is a bug: hands_on + supervising collapses 5 minutes of typing and
17 of an agent running into 'you spent 22 minutes', which is false about both
halves. DIVIDING across them is not: summed / unioned is precisely
meanConcurrency, the honest form of what a naive sum reports by accident. So
the pairs below are distinct quantities and the guard bans + and - between
them, never division.
Which quantities are elapsed time -- the union of underlying intervals, safe
to render as 'where your week went' -- and which are summed agent-hours. A
surface that quotes a summed figure as elapsed time is the specific defect
the elapsed/summed split exists to prevent.

concurrencyPairs.$comment: summed / unioned is meanConcurrency for this pair. Division legal, addition not.
